name: Museo del Prado
blurb: One of the finest art collections in the world: Spanish masters such as Velázquez and Goya, plus Flemish painters like Rubens.
priceText: €15 adults; free for children and students under 25 per Wikivoyage (conditions not checked)

name: Palacio Real
blurb: One of Europe's largest palaces, facing the Almudena Cathedral; the official royal residence, though the family lives elsewhere.
priceText: Entry €11; students and children €6; free M–Th 16:00–18:00 (Oct–Mar) for EU citizens and residents with ID (Wikivoyage)

name: Museo Nacional Centro de Arte Reina Sofía
blurb: Spain's largest 20th-century art collection, including Picasso's Guernica, in a former hospital with a modern wing.
priceText: €12 adults; free Mon and Wed–Sat 19:00–21:00 and Sun 13:30–19:00 (Wikivoyage)

name: Templo de Debod
blurb: Free Egyptian temple given to Spain for helping save Abu Simbel, set in a park near the Royal Palace.

name: Chocolatería San Ginés
blurb: Churros and thick chocolate at a Madrid fixture open 24 hours; a classic way to end a night out.

name: Mercado de San Ildefonso
blurb: Street-food market on Fuencarral in Malasaña with about 15 stalls: arepas, tacos, tapas, ham, wine and beer.

name: El Junco Jazz Club
blurb: Small jazz club that turns into a relaxed nightclub later on; entry prices include a drink and the crowd skews older.

name: Joy
blurb: Well-known club playing mainstream dance music to a mixed crowd of tourists and locals; Thursdays are a students' party.

name: Essential Flamenco
blurb: Authentic flamenco show in a 19th-century brick cellar; shows at 18:00, 19:30 and 21:00, with a free drink included.

name: Palacio de Hielo
blurb: Madrid's only year-round ice rink, in a northern mall that also has bowling, minigolf, a swimming pool and a cinema.

name: Catedral de Santa María de València
blurb: Former Roman temple, then a Visigothic church and Moorish mosque; the current Gothic cathedral was begun in 1262.

name: Ciutat de les Arts i les Ciències
blurb: Calatrava's futuristic complex on the old Turia riverbed; the combined ticket is pricey, so pick individual sections.
priceText: Combined admission, mid season: €46.40 adults, €36.30 reduced; valid 3 days (Wikivoyage)

name: Museu de Belles Arts de València
blurb: Free 17th-century palace museum with over 2,000 works, strongest in 14th–17th-century art and medieval altarpieces.

name: Museu de Prehistòria de València
blurb: Free regional prehistory museum covering the Paleolithic to the Visigoths, with the Warrior of Moixent bronze.

name: Mercat Central
blurb: One of Europe's largest markets, in a 1928 modernist iron-and-glass hall; fresh produce, meat, seafood and olives.

name: Kiosco La Pérgola
blurb: Lunch kiosk famous for huge bocadillos, including the Super Bombon with steak, jamón and fries.

name: La Fábrica de Hielo
blurb: Former ice factory with nightly concerts by local musicians, plus drinks and tapas; Sundays are devoted to jazz.

name: Café del Duende
blurb: Intimate flamenco café with well-known dancers; the €10 ticket includes a drink, and performances start at 23:00 Thu–Sat.

name: L'Oceanogràfic
blurb: Europe's largest oceanarium, shaped like a water lily by Félix Candela, with seven ecological zones.

name: Alcazaba
blurb: Best-preserved Moorish castle in Spain, built in the 11th century on a hill; the ramparts give views over the city.
priceText: General €7; reduced €3 (European Youth Card holders, EU citizens with student proof, 65+); free Sundays from 14:00 (official price list)

name: Picasso Museum
blurb: Paintings and artworks by the Málaga-born artist; your ticket also covers rotating exhibitions by other artists.

name: Málaga Cathedral
blurb: Cathedral in the city centre; open every day, but on Sundays only from 14:00.

name: Malaga Aviation Museum
blurb: Free museum in a 1940s airport terminal, with old aircraft, uniforms and airport models; fun for kids too.

name: Central Market (Mercado Central de Atarazanas)
blurb: Lively 19th-century wrought-iron market with regional produce, olive oil, fish, meat and cheese.

name: Restaurante Gallego Candamil
blurb: Galician restaurant popular with locals; cheap tapas such as empanada, with a glass of cider for little.
priceText: Tapa of empanada €1.25, glass of cider €1.15 (Wikivoyage)

name: Central Beers
blurb: Belgian beer bar with a good range of Belgian brews; busy at weekends.

name: Birras Deluxe
blurb: Belgian and American-style beers on tap, friendly staff, and food available.

name: Escapada Cycling
blurb: Gravel, e-bike, trekking and mountain bike rental, plus guided cycling experiences.

name: Sightseeing Treasure Hunt Málaga
blurb: Sightseeing treasure hunt with a bag of clues and a treasure book; by appointment, tours last at least 2.5 hours.
when: By appointment; tours at least 2.5 hours

name: Catedral de Sevilla
blurb: Huge 15th-century cathedral on the site of the former great mosque; Christopher Columbus's tomb lies inside.
priceText: €13 online, €14 at ticket office; students up to 25: €7 online, €8 at office (official; proof required)

name: Real Alcázar
blurb: Mudéjar royal palace from the 12th century, remodelled in the 14th; lavish gardens and richly decorated rooms.
priceText: Adult €13.50, concessions €6, plus Royal Apartments €4.50 (Wikivoyage; winter hours on official page)

name: Metropol Parasol
blurb: Giant wooden structure over the old town, designed by Jürgen Mayer-Hermann; locals call it 'las setas'.

name: Museo de Bellas Artes de Sevilla
blurb: Considered by some Spain's second fine-arts museum after the Prado, in a former convent with 15 rooms.
when: 1 Sep–31 Jul Tue–Sat 09:00–21:00; Sun and holidays 09:00–15:00

name: El Rinconcillo
blurb: Seville's oldest tavern: try the spinach with chickpeas or salmorejo while bartenders chalk the bill on the bar.

name: El Librero Tapas y Quesos
blurb: Cheese and ham tapas bar popular with locals; cheap tapas and a daily set menu.

name: La Carbonería
blurb: Bar with free flamenco shows every night at 21:30, 22:30 and 23:30; arrive early for seats.

name: Cafe-Bar Las Teresas
blurb: Lively cured-ham bar open late, popular with both locals and tourists.

name: Museo del Baile Flamenco
blurb: Flamenco museum in an 18th-century building in Santa Cruz, with sensory exhibits and evening performances.
priceText: Museum €10 adult, €8 senior, €6 child; performances €20 adults (Wikivoyage)

name: Castell de la Santa Bàrbara
blurb: Muslim-built fortress on Mount Benacantil, 166 m up, with huge views over the town and harbour. Free.

name: Museu Arqueològic Provincial d'Alacant (MARQ)
blurb: Provincial archaeology museum in a converted hospital, with an avant-garde design and strong regional finds.
priceText: €6 weekdays, €3 Sundays and holidays; reduced €3 for students, Carnet Jove holders and over-65s (official tariffs; proof required)

name: Museu de Belles Arts Gravina (MUBAG)
blurb: Free fine-arts museum in an 18th-century palace, with Spanish artworks displayed over three floors.
when: 1 Sep–30 Jun Tue–Sat 10:00–20:00; Sun and holidays 10:00–14:00

name: Museu d'Art Contemporani d'Alacant (MACA)
blurb: Free modern-art museum with works by Picasso, Braque, Miró and Juan Gris, plus two local artists.

name: Mercat Central (Alicante)
blurb: Two levels of meat, seafood, cheese, fruit and vegetables, with flower sellers in a small square at the back.

name: El Nou Cisne
blurb: Simple tapas and raciones bar with a set menu; the €11.90 price dates from 2016, so check it on arrival.

name: Sala Stereo
blurb: Concert venue for about 280 people with indie, rock and electronic music; Friday and Saturday DJ sessions.
when: DJ sessions Fri and Sat from 03:30

name: Sala The One
blurb: Large venue for around 1,000 with rock, punk and post-punk concerts and club nights; popular with students.

name: Coves del Canelobre
blurb: Large cave network with stalactites and one of Spain's highest vaults, a day trip inland from Alicante.
when: 1 Sep–30 Jun Tue–Fri 10:30–16:50; Sat, Sun, holidays 10:30–17:50; closed 25 Dec and 1 Jan

name: Palma Cathedral (La Seu)
blurb: Gothic cathedral begun in 1229; Gaudí tried to improve it and quit, and the Royal Chapel holds royal tombs.

name: Royal Palace of La Almudaina
blurb: Fortress with Roman roots and a 1309 rebuild; its upper floor holds grand 16th-century state rooms.
priceText: Adult €8, concession €5 (Wikivoyage; official ticket page showed no prices)

name: Castell de Bellver
blurb: Unusual circular 14th-century castle built over a Moorish fort; it withstood two sieges and holds a museum.

name: Banys Àrabs
blurb: Tenth-century bathhouse with under-floor heating, the only building in Palma from the Arab period; small and cheap.

name: Calixto
blurb: Paella is the whole menu, and it's good; a simple place to eat the dish in Palma.

name: Boira Restaurante
blurb: Mediterranean cooking at good value, served from breakfast until late evening.

name: Abaco
blurb: Over-the-top cocktail bar in a former coaching house with no food; on Fridays the music builds to a crescendo.

name: Gibson Bar
blurb: City-centre bar named in Wikivoyage's December nightlife tips; the source gives no hours or prices.

name: Palma Aquarium
blurb: Aquarium of Mediterranean and coastal ecosystems with a huge shark tank and many live corals; booking advised.

name: Catedral de Santa Ana
blurb: Cathedral visible from almost anywhere in the centre; building began in 1497 and mixes Gothic and Baroque styles.

name: Casa de Colón (Columbus House Museum)
blurb: House where Columbus stayed while his ships were refitted for his first voyage to the West Indies.

name: CAAM (Centro Atlántico de Arte Moderno)
blurb: Free modern-art museum in the former Banco de España building, with about 2,500 works from Europe, Africa and the Americas.

name: Castillo de la Luz
blurb: 16th-century fort built against pirates, now a rose garden with a cultural centre and a shipping museum.

name: Poema del Mar
blurb: Aquarium opened in 2018 with jungle, reef-beach and deep-ocean zones; big rays and sharks up close.

name: Playa de Las Canteras
blurb: Almost 4 km of city beach, the city's symbol; the golden-sand northern end is good for a swim at low tide.

name: Mercado Central (Las Palmas)
blurb: Central market with a large selection of fish and seafood.

name: La Candella
blurb: Good wood-fired pizzas, to eat in or take away; around €10 each.

name: Bar San Remo
blurb: Cozy bar with pool and darts, indoor and outdoor seating; beers about €2.50 and cocktails around €5.

name: NYC TAXI RockBar
blurb: Bar with blues and rock music, also serving hamburgers and sandwiches.

name: Museum of Nature and Archaeology (Tenerife)
blurb: Major museum of pre-Castilian Guanche objects, plus paleontology, botany and marine collections.

name: Palmetum
blurb: 120,000 m² palm botanical garden on an artificial hill over the ocean, with streams, ponds and a palm museum.
priceText: Non-resident adult €6; residents €3 with proof; non-resident children €2.80; under 3 free (official tariffs)

name: Jardín de Orquídeas Sitio Litre
blurb: 18th-century English-style garden with a large orchid collection, bonsai and a dragon tree.

name: García Sanabria Park
blurb: Free urban park from 1926, the largest in the Canaries, with fountains and a floral clock.

name: Loro Parque
blurb: World-class zoo that began as a parrot park; big cats, apes, an aquarium and the island's only roller coaster.
priceText: Adult €42, child 6–11 €30; car parking €7 (Wikivoyage; official site blocked)

name: Lago Martiánez
blurb: César Manrique's seawater pool and sunbathing complex in Puerto de la Cruz; very cheap to enter.

name: La Recova
blurb: Covered neocolonial market from 1943 in Santa Cruz, with fresh produce and fish; free to enter.

name: Mesón Los Gemelos
blurb: Popular Canarian restaurant with friendly service; weekend queues are long, so reservations are recommended.

name: Plaza Charco
blurb: Historic central square in Puerto de la Cruz with a fountain, surrounded by bars and restaurants.

name: Vinoteca Con Pasión
blurb: Gastropub and tapas bar with better-quality food than typical tapas spots, in Puerto de la Cruz.

name: Castelo de São Jorge
blurb: Hilltop castle above Alfama with views over the city; the site has been fortified since ancient times.
priceText: Adult €17; youth ages 13–25 €8.50 (proof required); children up to 12 free (official ticket page)

name: Calouste Gulbenkian Museum
blurb: One of Lisbon's best museums: Egyptian artefacts, Islamic and oriental art, and paintings by European masters.
priceText: Adult price not stated in source; reduced for ages 13–30 and 65+, free for ages 0–12 (Wikivoyage)

name: Panteão Nacional
blurb: Striking domed national pantheon in Alfama, with a rooftop terrace and excellent views over the city.

name: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
blurb: Highest viewpoint in Lisbon, on Graça hill beside a small chapel founded in 1147.

name: Time Out Market
blurb: Gourmet food hall in a former late-19th-century market, with about 40 kiosks, many run by well-known Lisbon chefs.

name: Pastéis de Belém
blurb: The famous custard-tart shop: pastries served warm from the oven with icing sugar and cinnamon.

name: Lux Fragil
blurb: Club in a former warehouse, open Thursday to Sunday until 06:00.

name: Tasca do Chico
blurb: Cramped but authentic Fado bar in Bairro Alto.

name: Lisboa em Fado
blurb: Fado concert hall with daily shows of about an hour, run by a young Lisbon guitarist.

name: Monsanto Forest Park
blurb: Protected municipal forest of almost 10 km², the city's largest green patch, with an interpretation centre.

name: Palácio da Bolsa
blurb: Stock Exchange Palace: the Arab Room is the highlight, plus a port-wine tasting room.
priceText: Individual €14; reduced €9.50 for students, school groups and seniors (official page)

name: Fundação de Serralves
blurb: Contemporary museum by Álvaro Siza, with a large park, an Art Deco villa and a restaurant.
priceText: €8.50 museum and park; €4 park only; free Sundays 10:00–13:00 for students and under-18s; 50% off 65+ and Porto card holders (Wikivoyage)

name: Livraria Lello
blurb: Ornate bookshop with a spiral staircase, voted among Europe's most beautiful; very crowded inside.
priceText: €10 online ticket, €12 at the entrance; the ticket can be used towards books (Wikivoyage)

name: Centro Português de Fotografia
blurb: Free photography museum in a beautiful building in the city centre.

name: Mercado do Bolhão
blurb: Traditional market of fruit, vegetables, fish and meat, fully reopened after major refurbishment in 2022.

name: Casa das Tortas
blurb: Homemade Portuguese food and bakery pastries; Wikivoyage calls its francesinha the best in Porto.

name: Prioridade Bar
blurb: Ribeira bar where a large beer costs only a few euros, one of the cheapest in the area.
priceText: Large beer for only a few euros (Wikivoyage)

name: Industria
blurb: Dance club running since 1987, open until around 06:00.

name: Douro river cruise
blurb: About 50-minute boat trip upriver on the Douro; most operators sail every 30 minutes between 10:00 and 18:30.

name: Fado Bars (Porto)
blurb: Traditional fado sung by a woman in a black dress with guitar players; a handful of fado bars in Porto.
